title: Unreal past, wishes / contrast
subtitle: Past tenses for unreal situations, wish / if only, and contrast linkers

blocks.text: Past tenses do not always refer to past time. In some sentences and with some verbs or phrases we use a past tense to refer to the present or the future, or to a general situation. These include sentences that contain:

rows.example: I'd buy that jacket if I **had** more cash on me.
I know it's probably not going to happen but **suppose / imagine** I **became** a famous designer! **What if** I **became** a famous designer?

rows.use: would rather + you / he / she / we / they
rows.example: I'd rather you **didn't come** with me to the fashion show tomorrow.
It's **(high / about) time** that hats **came** back in fashion.
**Did** you **want** me to send you our new catalogue when it comes out?
**If only** I **had** something to wear tonight.

blocks.text: **Suppose**, **what if** and **imagine** can also be followed by a present tense. A present tense indicates that the situation is more likely to actually happen. A past tense indicates that the situation is less likely to actually happen.

blocks.correct: **What if** you **are** accepted into art college? (more likely to happen)
blocks.incorrect: What if you will be accepted into art college?

items: **What if** you **were** accepted into art college? (less likely to happen)

blocks.text: We use different structures with **wish** / **if only**, depending on exactly what we want to express.

rows.statement: wish / if only + past simple / continuous
rows.negative: I **wish I was studying** history of fashion instead of biology!
rows.question: a wish about now or generally

rows.statement: wish / if only + past perfect simple / continuous
rows.negative: **If only I'd known** Burton's was having a sale last week.
rows.question: regret about a past situation

rows.negative: I **wish I could** fit into these jeans.
rows.question: hypothetical ability now or generally

rows.negative: I **wish to try on** this ball gown.
rows.question: a formal way to say what you want

blocks.text: We do not formally say **If only / I wish I would…** for wishes about ourselves. Use a past tense or **could** instead.

blocks.correct: **If only / I wish I had** enough money to buy these shoes.
blocks.incorrect: If only / I wish I would have enough money to buy these shoes.

blocks.correct: **If only / I wish I could** afford these shoes.
blocks.incorrect: If only / I wish I would afford these shoes.

blocks.text: To express desires about the future, we often use **hope**, not **wish** + **will**.

blocks.correct: I **hope I will** have enough money to buy these shoes next week.
blocks.incorrect: I wish I will have enough money to buy these shoes next week.

blocks.text: **Although**, **though** and **even though** are used to express contrast. **Even though** is more emphatic than **although** and **though**. **Though** is more informal than **although** and **even though**.

rows.use: Although / Though / Even though + subject + verb, subject + verb
rows.example: **Although / Though / Even though** I wore a hat, I got sunburn.

rows.use: subject + verb, although / though / even though + subject + verb
rows.example: I got sunburn, **although / though / even though** I wore a hat.

blocks.text: **Though** can also come at the end of a sentence.
blocks.note: I wore a hat. I got sunburn, **though**.

blocks.text: **In spite of** and **despite** are used to express contrast. They mean exactly the same thing and take the same grammatical structures.

rows.use: in spite of / despite + -ing form, subject + verb
rows.example: **In spite of / Despite wearing** a hat, I got sunburn.

rows.use: in spite of / despite + the fact (that) + subject + verb, subject + verb
rows.example: **In spite of / Despite the fact (that)** I wore a hat, I got sunburn.

rows.use: in spite of / despite + noun, subject + verb
rows.example: **In spite of / Despite** my hat, I got sunburn.

blocks.text: We can also put **in spite of / despite** in the middle of the sentence.
blocks.note: I got sunburn **in spite of / despite** wearing a hat.

blocks.intro: We can also use the perfect **-ing** form to show that the action happened before the result.
items: I got sunburn **in spite of / despite having worn** a hat.

blocks.text: With **in spite of / despite** + **-ing** form, the subject of the main verb must also carry out the action of the **-ing** verb.

blocks.incorrect: My sunburn was terrible in spite of / despite wearing a hat. (= My sunburn wore a hat!)

blocks.text: **However** and **nevertheless** are used to express contrast. **However** is formal. **Nevertheless** is even more formal.

items: The fashion show was expensive to put on. **However / Nevertheless**, it did make a profit.
The fashion show was expensive to put on. It did, **however / nevertheless**, make a profit.
The fashion show was expensive to put on. It did make a profit, **however / nevertheless**.

blocks.text: **While** and **whereas** are used to contrast two different facts or ideas.

rows.use: while / whereas + subject + verb, subject + verb
rows.example: **While / Whereas** jeans are worn by both men and women, blouses are worn only by women.

rows.use: subject + verb, while / whereas + subject + verb
rows.example: Blouses are worn only by women, **while / whereas** jeans are worn by both men and women.

exercises.title: D · Keep the meaning
exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence so that the meaning remains the same.

items.prompt:
I don't like your criticising me all the time.
**I wish**
acceptedAnswers: I wish you wouldn't criticise me all the time.
I wish you wouldn't criticize me all the time.
I wish you didn't criticise me all the time.

items.prompt:
It's awful — Sam doesn't know how I feel about him!
**If only**
acceptedAnswers: If only Sam knew how I feel about him!
If only Sam knew how I felt about him!

items.prompt:
I'd love to be with you in Switzerland right now.
**I wish**
acceptedAnswers: I wish I was with you in Switzerland right now.
I wish I were with you in Switzerland right now.
I wish I could be with you in Switzerland right now.

items.prompt:
Frank regrets not taking the job when he had the chance.
**Frank wishes**
acceptedAnswers: Frank wishes he had taken the job when he had the chance.
Frank wishes he'd taken the job when he had the chance.

items.prompt:
Wouldn't you like us to be standing in the middle of Times Square right now?
**Don't you wish**
acceptedAnswers: Don't you wish we were standing in the middle of Times Square right now?
Don't you wish we could be standing in the middle of Times Square right now?

items.prompt:
It's a shame I can't play chess as well as Steve.
**I wish**
acceptedAnswers: I wish I could play chess as well as Steve.
I wish I played chess as well as Steve.

items.prompt:
What would you do if you had a million euros?
**Suppose**
acceptedAnswers: Suppose you had a million euros, what would you do?
Suppose you had a million euros. What would you do?

items.prompt:
I don't really want you to smoke in here.
**I'd rather**
acceptedAnswers: I'd rather you didn't smoke in here.
I'd rather you did not smoke in here.

items.prompt:
It's time for them to go to bed.
**It's high time**
acceptedAnswers: It's high time they went to bed.
It's high time they went to bed

exercises.title: E · Finish the contrast sentence
exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence so that it contrasts being a vegetarian with occasionally eating fish. Write the missing words.

items.prompt: **Although** Aesop is a vegetarian, ___
**Despite** ___, Aesop does occasionally eat fish.
acceptedAnswers: the fact that he is a vegetarian

items.prompt: **Despite the fact that Aesop is a vegetarian**, ___
Aesop is a vegetarian, ___.
acceptedAnswers: although he does occasionally eat fish

items.prompt: **Despite his vegetarianism**, ___
**In spite of** ___, Aesop does occasionally eat fish.
acceptedAnswers: the fact that he is a vegetarian

items.prompt: **Despite having** ___ for years, Aesop does occasionally eat fish.
Aesop is a vegetarian. **However**, ___
Aesop is a vegetarian. He does occasionally eat fish, ___.

exercises.title: G · Key word transformation
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence. Write between two and five words in each gap.

items.prompt:
Although he was exhausted, Mike kept on climbing. **fact**
In ___ he was exhausted, Mike kept on climbing.

Sally had been sure she would win the music competition. She came third, however. **been**
Despite ___ would win the music competition, Sally came third.

Doug wasn't shortlisted for the job even though he had a great CV. **spite**
Doug wasn't shortlisted for the job ___ a great CV.

Planes can still take off and land but ferries have been cancelled. **whereas**
Ferries have been cancelled, ___ able to take off and land.

Despite having got a good degree, Sandra couldn't find a well-paid job. **even**
Sandra couldn't find a well-paid job ___ a good degree.

Even though he'd been robbed twice, Red still enjoyed living in the city. **having**
Red still enjoyed living in the city ___ twice.
acceptedAnswers: in spite of having been robbed

items.prompt:
It's a great film despite the plot being a little complicated. **though**
It's a great film, ___ a little complicated.

Despite looking everywhere, the kids failed to find the tennis ball. **although**
The kids failed to find the tennis ball ___ everywhere.

In ___ , Pat really enjoyed the match.

Despite ___ , the police didn't manage to catch the culprit.
